description: All system bugs. Each bug has its own environment and status attributes. Environments constrained to local/dev/qa/prod. Source of truth for defect tracking.

bug.title: Multiple disjoint stores for build/version/framework data
bug.description: Build, version, and framework identifiers are currently stored across at least three patterns: (1) per-environment Mongo collection {ENV_PREFIX}_System.version (read by /health endpoints in FindCare/EvaluateCare/SharedServices and consumed by the env banner); (2) global admin.framework_version Mongo collection (managed by Code/Shared/ops/framework_version.py); (3) flat file brain/machine_artifacts/content/version.json (read by conversation_log_consumer.py for record stamping, by boot_probe.py for session-start logging, by conversation_log_purge_service.py, and copied into the docker stage by deploy_localhost_docker.sh). A fourth pattern, {db}.build_counter, is referenced in older design docs. EPIC-008-F-007-S-006-REQ-T-008 explicitly contradicts the Mongo-based path by mandating reads 'from version.json'. EPIC-006-F-009-S-004-REQ-T-004 ('All database names must use ENV_PREFIX') is silently violated by the existing global admin.* collections. Result: no single source of truth, denormalized data, drift risk, and at least one direct requirement contradiction. | Authored Rule-063 (build-bump on post-commit) into engineering_rules.json with body and statements but with an empty enforcements.enforcement array — schema-noncompliant pending the migration of Code/Shared/ops/bump_build.py from a deploy-time CLI (currently called with --env from 5 GitHub workflows: deploy-findcare-website-dev/qa, deploy-pipelines, promote-build, promote-data) into a post-commit enforcement worker that calls the canonical bump primitive and pushes the new build value to the running Kafka producer.
pytest_success_criteria: After a non-deploy commit, the build field of the canonical version document in MongoDB is incremented by exactly one
version.json file does not exist in the repository
No production code reads version.json (grep returns empty)
Banner displays correct build/version/framework values from /health
Smoke test passes against local and dev environments
Conversation-log records carry _build/_version/_framework fields stamped by the producer

Rule-063 in engineering_rules.json has at least one enforcement entry conforming to schema (enforcement_id, hook, executable_path with minLength 1, requires_lock all populated) and the bump-build worker the entry points to is wired into the post-commit hook chain.
bug.reproduction: 1. Inspect MongoDB collections {ENV}_System.version and admin.framework_version. 2. Inspect file brain/machine_artifacts/content/version.json. 3. Verify that build/version/framework data lives in all three locations with no automated mechanism keeping them in sync. 4. Read EPIC-008-F-007-S-006-REQ-T-008 and EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-T-002 — note the contradiction.
next_action: Define canonical Mongo collection (extend admin.framework_version or successor)
Create one canonical engineering rule (Rule-063) with an enforcement on post-commit that increments build on non-deploy commits
Write a Python routine Claude invokes when version or framework needs updating (no separate CLI ceremony)
Both writers push new values to producer; producer caches as static
Producer stamps Kafka messages with version; consumer copies through
Update boot_probe.py and conversation_log_consumer.py to drop version.json read
Delete version.json file and all references
Delete EPIC-008-F-007-S-006-REQ-T-008
Delete conversation_log_purge_service.py

Migrate bump_build.py: drop the --env arg, retarget it at the canonical Mongo collection and the canonical document/field names, remove the 5 GitHub workflow calls (deploys no longer bump), then create the thin enforcement worker that wraps it and pushes to the Kafka producer; finally fill in Rule-063 enforcement entry pointing at that worker.

Spawn audit agent: enumerate all rogue artifacts across the repo (Mongo collections via live connection, code references with broader name variants, config files, GitHub workflow inputs, generated files) AND all rogue requirements in agile_backlog.json that touch build/version/framework storage; present findings as a single inventory for human review.
Spawn cleanup agent: act on the inventory from the audit agent (delete rogue collections, code references, configs, requirements) once human-approved; report what was changed.

bug.title: Git-eligible artifacts hardcode absolute paths instead of using {project root}
bug.description: Git-eligible artifacts across the repo (any file tracked or trackable in git — code, configs, scripts, generators, docs, JSON, YAML) hardcode absolute filesystem paths (most commonly 'c:\chatHealthy indCare', the legacy project tree) instead of resolving paths from a project-root reference (env var CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT or computed via Path(__file__).parents[N]). Concrete impact: (1) the C# supervisor Code/CSharp/ChatHealthyLogService/dev/Worker.cs launches producer/consumer from the legacy tree, so code changes to the new project (c:\CHATHealthyLLC) do not affect any running process — this specific instance was fixed in this session by env-var-driven Worker.cs + system env var CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT; (2) start_local.bat launches all four local services from the legacy tree; (3) the boot class chathealthy_devops_boot.py (governs every Claude session) carries a legacy-path marker; (4) at least 12 other Git-eligible artifacts (rebuild_manifest.py, bash_rule_guard.py, build_backlog_story_view.py, both conversation_log_agent copies, daily_conversation_commit.sh, gen_ops_design_docx.py, generate_log_refactor_plan.py, etc.) carry the same defect. On 2026-05-01 Skip attempted to rename c:/chatHealthy/findCare and the rename failed because the supervisor-spawned Python processes had open handles in that tree. Per Skip 2026-05-01: the C# service was always a bit of an anomaly and the broader sweep may find fewer hits than the audit suggests.
pytest_success_criteria: grep for 'c:\chathealthy\findcare' (case-insensitive) across Git-eligible artifacts returns zero hits (excluding test_output/, _pending/, scratch dirs that are themselves slated for removal or gitignored)
Every Git-eligible artifact resolves its project root via either os.environ['CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT'] or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N], not from a hardcoded absolute path
C# Worker.cs files take RepoRoot from environment/configuration, not as a const

Restarting the supervisor causes the running producer/consumer to load code from the project root configured in the supervisor environment, verified by hitting /version_bump (which exists only in the new tree) and getting 200
Renaming or moving c:/chatHealthy/findCare succeeds without OS file-lock errors (no process holds handles there)
bug.reproduction: 1. Run grep -rln -iE 'c:[\/]chathealthy[\/]findcare' from repo root across Git-eligible artifacts; observe at least 12 hits. 2. Try to rename c:/chatHealthy/findCare; observe failure due to file locks held by supervisor-spawned processes (PIDs visible via tasklist + netstat -ano on port 8100).
next_action: Spawn audit agent: enumerate every Git-eligible artifact with a hardcoded absolute path; produce inventory grouped by file role (supervisor, launcher, tool, generator, doc, etc.).

Spawn cleanup agent: migrate each file in the inventory to use {project root} (env var CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT or Path(__file__).parents[N]); rebuild C# supervisor; restart services; verify by re-running BUG-001's SIT.

Spawn placement-recommendation agent: parse every epic, every feature, every story, and every requirement in agile_backlog.json; recommend the structural home (which epic / feature / story) for a new requirement mandating 'Git-eligible artifacts MUST NOT contain hardcoded absolute filesystem paths and MUST resolve the project root via environment variable or computed-relative path.' Output: recommendation with rationale for Skip's review.
Skip authors the requirement at the recommended location.
Add engineering rule (anchored to the new requirement) that forbids hardcoded absolute paths and enforces project-root resolution.
After fix lands: BUG-001 SIT can run to completion (this bug unblocks that one).

bug.title: EPIC-008-F-004 Feachure fails to comply with the Fail-hard requirement
bug.description:
SCOPE: EPIC-008-F-004 (DevOps — Build, Deploy, and Environment Management) only. All findings below are confined to the three files owned by this feature: Code/deploy/local_deploy.py, Code/deploy/remote_deploy.py, and Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py. This bug does not assert violations in any other feature's surface area. The umbrella requirement is EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-B-001 (atomic deploy / fail-hard / no half-deployed third state); each invented path below produces exactly the prohibited third state.

On 2026-05-01 the V11 EPIC-008-F-004 design committed to five constraints, including #5: 'No invention; meet V11 exactly, nothing more, nothing less.' V11 S-002-REQ-T-001 specifies that local backend services run as Docker containers built from each backend's Dockerfile and requirements.txt, with the runtime forbidden from importing any package not installed by the container's pip install. When I implemented Code/deploy/local_deploy.py overnight, I probed Docker once at ~22:50, got 'docker daemon not running,' and chose to invent a subprocess-Python fallback path: _build_backend_containers() became a no-op that logs 'SKIPPED — V11 deviation, bug filed,' and _start_backend_processes() shells out to Code/deploy/_start_*.py launchers running against the host venv. Filing the deviation as a known bug did not unwrite the invention — it papered over it. The correct V11-faithful options were (a) implement Docker per spec, or (b) refuse to deploy locally until Docker is up. The subprocess-Python path is neither. The substantive risk is drift between local and deployed envs: subprocess Python imports from C:\CHATHealthyLLC\.venv (whatever the developer happened to install), while dev/qa/prod backends run in HuggingFace Docker SDK Spaces with packages drawn strictly from each backend's requirements.txt. Local SIT can pass with a package set that does not exist in any deployed env (extra packages installed in the developer's venv mask import errors; missing packages can be paper-imported from a global site-packages). The local smoke test therefore does not faithfully validate what deploys to dev/qa/prod, defeating the purpose of running it. Subsequent audit on 2026-05-02 surfaced five additional invented paths of the same shape across the same overnight commits: (1) LocalDeploy._validate_prerequisites() falls back to shutil.copytree(ux_target, ux_link) when mklink fails — copy is not symlink and creates drift; (2) RemoteDeploy._verify_target_hf_space() logs 'Space may not exist yet — workflow will create' and continues when an HF Space is unreachable, treating soft-fail as success against V11 S-001-REQ-B-002 (verifies the target environment is reachable); (3) RemoteDeploy._verify_cloudflare_settings() records pass/fail in the structured output but does not gate the deploy and does not implement the 'configures it if absent' half of V11 S-003-REQ-T-002/T-003; (5) TestStep35::test_step35b_mtls_full_mesh calls pytest.skip() when MTLS_ENABLED=False — V11 S-006-REQ-T-003 makes no provision for skipping based on env-level mTLS toggle; the skip was invented; (9) LocalDeploy.main() accepts an invented --no-smoke convenience flag that V11 does not authorize and that violates the atomic-deploy guarantee of S-001-REQ-B-001 (succeeds totally or fails totally). All same disease as the original Docker fallback, all show_stoppers under the standing rule.
pytest_success_criteria: Code/deploy/local_deploy.py contains NO subprocess-Python fallback path for backend services. The methods _build_backend_containers() and _start_backend_processes() either do real Docker work or fail loudly — there is no third state.

If the Docker daemon is unreachable when LocalDeploy.run() executes, the run aborts with an explicit, terminal error (non-zero exit, clear message: 'Docker daemon required per V11 S-002-REQ-T-001'). It does NOT fall back to subprocess Python.
_build_backend_containers() invokes `docker build` for each of the 3 backend services (idempotent if the image is up to date) producing images ch-findcare, ch-evalcare, ch-sharedsvc.

_start_backend_processes() invokes `docker start ch-findcare`, `docker start ch-evalcare`, `docker start ch-sharedsvc` (with `docker run` fallback ONLY for the case where the named container does not yet exist; this is normal Docker workflow, not a V11-violating fallback).
After local deploy: `docker ps` shows ch-findcare, ch-evalcare, ch-sharedsvc running; `tasklist | findstr python.exe` shows zero processes from the legacy _start_*.py launchers.

Each container's pip-installed package set equals exactly the corresponding backend's requirements.txt (verified by `docker exec <container> pip list` set-equal to requirements.txt — neither extra packages nor missing ones); this is the parity guarantee that makes local SIT a real test of dev/qa/prod behavior.

Code/deploy/_start_findcare.py, _start_evalcare.py, _start_shared.py are deleted (they only existed to support the subprocess-Python fallback; with that path removed they are dead code that would invite re-violation).
Code/deploy/_start_website.py remains (the Website wrapper is host-OS per V11 S-002-REQ-T-002, which is a separate intentional non-Docker requirement).

Master smoke test (localSmokeTestPyTest.py with --smoke-env=local) runs against the Docker-containerized backends and produces a result. The pass/fail count of that result is recorded as the new local SIT baseline (it MAY differ from the subprocess-Python baseline because the package sets differ — that is the entire point of the fix; either result is valid as long as it reflects the real container behavior).
LocalDeploy._validate_prerequisites() does NOT copy the ux directory as a fallback when mklink fails. Either the symlink is created or the deploy aborts with terminal error.
RemoteDeploy._verify_target_hf_space() aborts hard if any expected HF Space is unreachable. No 'Space may not exist yet — workflow will create' silent continuation.

RemoteDeploy._verify_cloudflare_settings() aborts hard if HTTP→HTTPS or 404 verification fails AND implements the auto-configure half of V11 S-003-REQ-T-002/T-003 ('verifies and configures if absent') so the verification is paired with the configuration the spec mandates.

TestStep35::test_step35b_mtls_full_mesh does NOT use pytest.skip(). The mTLS-disabled vs mTLS-enabled distinction is declared at the smoke-test invocation level (different env config files, different test selection at the deploy-script call site), not as an in-test skip.
LocalDeploy.main() does NOT accept --no-smoke or any other flag that bypasses smoke. The deploy is atomic per V11 S-001-REQ-B-001 — there is no half-deploy mode.

LocalDeploy._pids_listening_on() and the kill loop in _teardown_precondition() do NOT silently swallow psutil.AccessDenied. A permission failure on kill is surfaced and aborts the deploy with a terminal error (V11 S-001-REQ-T-005 — the wipe is the precondition; if we cannot wipe, we cannot deploy).

LocalDeploy._port_in_use() does NOT catch OSError/timeout and return False. A failure to determine port state is surfaced and aborts the deploy with a terminal error. The function returns True/False only when it can actually tell.

LocalDeploy._verify_components() GATES the deploy. If any verification check fails, the deploy aborts with terminal error per V11 S-001-REQ-B-001 (atomic deploy / no half-deployed third state). It does NOT record pass/fail and continue to smoke.

RemoteDeploy._dispatch_workflow() does NOT silently swallow JSON parse or list-API failures. If the dispatched run cannot be tracked, the deploy aborts with terminal error — there is no untracked-but-running workflow.

TestStep06::test_search (line 395) does NOT silently swallow a missing 'Yes, keep waiting' button. The expected presence-or-absence of that button is declared in the test (either always present, with explicit assertion, or always absent, with explicit assertion). The Playwright pattern of suppressing an assertion to handle 'optional' UI is forbidden — suppressed assertions hide problems.
bug.reproduction: 1. Run `python Code/deploy/local_deploy.py --no-smoke`. 2. Observe step notice: 'backend containers SKIPPED — using subprocess Python (V11 S-002-REQ-T-001 deviation, bug filed)'. 3. Run `docker ps -a` and `docker image ls` — observe ch-findcare/ch-evalcare/ch-sharedsvc images and stopped containers exist on the machine, ready to use. 4. Run `tasklist | findstr python.exe` — observe 4 python.exe processes for the 4 _start_*.py launchers, NOT in any container. 5. Inspect Code/deploy/local_deploy.py:_build_backend_containers — confirm it is a no-op. 6. Re-read overnight commit message for c307f9c — confirm the 'V11 deviation' is acknowledged in the commit but never repaired.
next_action: Confirm Dockerfiles for findcare/evalcare/sharedservices exist; locate them. The presence of ch-* images in `docker image ls` implies a build process exists somewhere — find and align with V11.
Implement LocalDeploy._build_backend_containers() to invoke `docker build` per service (idempotent — `docker build` with --quiet returns instantly if cached).

Replace LocalDeploy._start_backend_processes() with `docker start` (creating containers via `docker run` if missing); preserve V11 port table mappings (7860, 8001, 8002 host-side) and cert volume mounts.
Add a Docker-availability precheck at the top of LocalDeploy.run(): `docker version` must succeed, else terminal abort with V11 reference.

Update LocalDeploy._teardown_precondition() to `docker stop ch-findcare ch-evalcare ch-sharedsvc` before any port-based process kill; explicitly preserve the chathealthy-kafka container (separate infrastructure).
Delete Code/deploy/_start_findcare.py, _start_evalcare.py, _start_shared.py (dead-code prevention for the deleted subprocess-Python path).
Re-run the master smoke test against Docker-backed local; record the new baseline pass/fail count and update agile_backlog.json req status accordingly.
Remove the ux-copytree fallback in LocalDeploy._validate_prerequisites(); fail hard on mklink error.
Make RemoteDeploy._verify_target_hf_space() abort the deploy if any HF Space is unreachable.

Make RemoteDeploy._verify_cloudflare_settings() abort the deploy if verification fails; implement the 'configure if absent' Cloudflare API path so V11 S-003-REQ-T-002/T-003 is fully met (currently only verify, not configure).
Remove pytest.skip from TestStep35::test_step35b_mtls_full_mesh; surface the mTLS-enabled-vs-not distinction at the smoke-test invocation contract, not as an in-test skip.
Remove --no-smoke from LocalDeploy.main(); deploy is atomic with no smoke-skip mode.

Remove the `except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied): pass` swallow in LocalDeploy._teardown_precondition; re-raise AccessDenied; treat NoSuchProcess as success (no longer running = goal achieved).
Change LocalDeploy._port_in_use to let OSError propagate; only ConnectionRefusedError counts as 'port free'. Timeout means we don't know — abort.
Add a hard gate at the end of LocalDeploy._verify_components: if any verification entry has ok=False, sys.exit with the failed checks listed.
Remove the `except Exception: pass` in RemoteDeploy._dispatch_workflow; re-raise to abort the dispatch step. Untracked workflow runs are not acceptable.

Remove the `except Exception: pass` around the 'Yes, keep waiting' button in localSmokeTestPyTest.py Step 06; either assert the button must be present (and click it) or assert it must be absent. The optional-element-with-suppressed-exception pattern is forbidden across the smoke test.
